About

Tomas Hidalgo · Río Arriba County, New Mexico

My name is Tomas Hidalgo. I am a carpenter. I live with my wife and a yellow dog named Inez on a small piece of land about an hour north of Santa Fe, on the high side of a county road that winds up out of the river valley and ends, eventually, at a forest gate. For seven years before this I lived in San Francisco and worked as an engineer at a company you have probably heard of, doing work that I cannot now, in good faith, describe to you. In the spring of 2019 I gave my notice. The decision took me four years to make and about four hours to act on, which is, I have come to believe, the usual ratio.

I build furniture, mostly — case pieces, the occasional table, now and then a door for a neighbor who is doing his own remodel and has run out of money and time. The shop is unheated and the tools are mostly older than I am. I take commissions a few times a year, never more than I can finish without hurrying, and the rest of the time I work on the property: the orchard, the fences, the acequia in season, the woodpile in any season at all. I am not particularly good at any of this yet. I am told it takes about twenty years to be honestly competent at country life, and I am six years in, which means I have at least fourteen left in which to be wrong about most things. I find this comforting.

I write one essay a month. I send it to a small list of readers on the morning of the new moon, which is an old habit I picked up from my grandmother, who timed her bread starters by the lunar calendar and lived to be ninety-four. The essays are about whatever I have been thinking about — usually some intersection of land and work and attention, occasionally an old grievance, occasionally a piece of advice I would rather have been given than have to give. I write slowly, by hand first, and I do not publish anything I cannot still defend a year later. This rules out a great deal.

I do not have a phone that does very much. I do not use social media. I am not for hire as a coach or a consultant or a speaker, and I have nothing to sell you. If you would like to write to me — and I do answer letters, eventually — the address is P.O. Box 47, Truchas, NM 87578. If a letter is too slow for what you want to say, the email is tomas@firstlight.example, and I check it on Thursday mornings, with coffee, before I go out to the shop. I cannot promise to be quick. I can promise to read carefully.

That is most of what there is to say. The rest is in the essays.
